q: Saharanpur foundries cast hand pumps on coke: what is the cluster's footprint?
title: Saharanpur foundries: hand pump castings CO2
short: Roughly 0.9 t CO2 per tonne of castings, about 18,700 t a year in all. Saharanpur's 50 working foundries made about 21,000 t from 4,100 t of coke and 9.3 million kWh. Coke gives two thirds of the CO2, and the smallest cupola units run far higher per tonne.
audience: Cupola foundries on Delhi Road, Mandi Samiti Road and Gagalheri in Saharanpur

ul: About 100 foundries exist; about 50 were working when TERI surveyed them.
Hand pump castings are 60% of output, sewing machine parts 25%, paper mill machinery 10%. Hand pumps also go to Nepal and Bhutan.
Nearly all melt in conventional cupolas of 2 to 4 t an hour, most over ten years old; only two use induction furnaces.
Coke is a mix of Dhanbad coke (about 24% ash) and Gujarat coke (about 12%), usually 60 to 70% Dhanbad.

p: A unit making 60 t of saleable castings a year uses a third of a tonne of coke per tonne, against about a fifth at 500 to 1,000 t. Coke runs at 20 to 25% of metal melted and 30 to 35% of good castings, so rejects and returns cost you twice.

ol: Bring rejects from 10 to 15% down below 5% with tighter process control.
Knock sand off runners and risers before remelting; it is 4 to 5% of their weight.
Size the blower to the cupola's inner diameter: about 5% less coke.
Fix charging and operating practice: 5 to 10%.
Then a divided blast cupola: about 100 kg of coke per tonne of liquid metal against 150 to 200 kg now, with payback inside a year on coke alone.

sections.h: What to send a pump buyer
p: Give CO2 per tonne of good castings, naming coke tonnes, kWh and factors, then per pump from the casting weight of each model.

example.title: Three unit sizes and the cluster (estimate)
lines: 60 t castings: 20 t coke x 3.02 = 60 t; 50,000 kWh x 0.675 = 34 t; 1.57 t CO2 per tonne
500 t: 110 t coke = 332 t; 200,000 kWh = 135 t; 0.93 t per tonne
1,000 t: 200 t coke = 604 t; 500,000 kWh = 338 t; 0.94 t per tonne
Cluster: 4,100 t coke = 12,382 t; 9.3 million kWh = 6,278 t; 18,660 t / 21,000 t = 0.89 t per tonne
example.note: Coke, power and output from TERI's cluster profile (2014-15). Coke at the IPCC default for coke oven coke; high ash coke carries less carbon per tonne, so a lab carbon result would refine this.

senseible: Put your coke tonnes and kWh into the calculators for a first figure per tonne; Senseible can then read each month's power bill and coke invoice into records you can show a buyer.
